subject: NimbleSecure MAP: integration sprint status, owners, and blockers
messages:
From: Alex Pierce <alex@nimblesecure.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nimblesecure.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MAP kickoff: integration checkpoints and owners

Hi Priyom / Monica,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — NimbleSecure is excited to move into a short MAP to validate the SDK and streaming integrations before contract signature. Attached is our initial target timeline and a short list of success criteria. We want weekly checkpoints focused on three tracks: SDK/API integration, auth/token flow, and streaming/tool calling.

Can you confirm owners on your side and whether you can supply the auth token spec by next Tuesday? Also please call out any known lift for streaming RTP/low-latency frames — we'll need that for our infra planning.

Attachments: nimble_integration_plan_v2.pdf (MAP outline), auth-token-specs.xlsx (current Nimble format)

Best,
Alex Pierce
Head of Integrations, NimbleSecure
alex@nimblesecure.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alex Pierce <alex@nimblesecure.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP kickoff: integration checkpoints and owners

Alex — thanks for the plan and the attachments. High-level reply and owners below: 

- SDK / API integration: priyom_das (owner) — main contact for client SDK onboarding and example apps.
- Auth / tokens: monica_patel (owner) — will validate token exchange and KMS expectations.
- Streaming & tool-calling: karthik_iyer (owner) — will validate low-latency path and tool call bindings.

We can produce an initial auth compatibility matrix by Tue 2026-10-20. That will include required headers, token rotation guidance, and recommended scopes.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the max allowed client concurrency and expected frame sizes for streaming? That drives batching and KV-cache sizing.
- Any compliance evidence we should attach to the MAP (SOC2 or architecture diagrams)?

I'll set up a recurring 30m checkpoint for Fridays at 10am PT starting 2026-10-16; please accept if that works.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a short agenda before the first check-in.

Best,
Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, Alex Pierce <alex@nimblesecure.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP kickoff: integration checkpoints and owners

Agenda for today's 10am PT checkpoint (recap + notes):

1) Quick status (5m) — SDK repo skeleton shared; NimbleSecure to confirm language binding (JS + Python).
2) Auth matrix (10m) — Monica to confirm token exchange plan and ask about KMS/HSM requirements.
3) Streaming (10m) — Karthik to outline latency baseline and required protocol (WebRTC vs custom TCP).
4) Next actions & owners (5m).

Meeting notes (live):
- Alex: Nimble will provide expected concurrency and frame sizes by EOD 10/16. (Action: Alex)
- Monica: Redwood will map Nimble token fields to Redwood's token introspection flow and flag missing fields by 10/20. (Action: Monica)
- Karthik: Redwood will run a quick smoke test for streaming with sample frames and report P50/P95 latencies by 10/19. (Action: Karthik)
- Priyom: create mutual action plan hub doc and add these action items + timelines. (Action: Priyom)

Blockers identified:
- Nimble's current token metadata uses a custom claim (ns_scope) that isn't in our default introspection schema. Monica to propose mapping or fallback.
- Streaming sample frames exceed 2MB per frame in one test case — needs clarification on whether compression is allowed.

Attachments referenced: nimble_integration_plan_v2.pdf (from Alex)

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, Alex Pierce <alex@nimblesecure.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP kickoff: integration checkpoints and owners

Quick tech update and action items after initial smoke run: 

- Smoke test run (10/17): SDK client connected, handshake + initial tokens OK. Observed P50=120ms, P95=420ms for 4 concurrent streams using our baseline encoding.
- Issue: large uncompressed frames cause transient memory pressure on the inference worker; we'll need either compression on the client or chunking. Recommendation: client-side gzip or a chunked frame format (suggest 256KB chunks).
- Auth: token introspection worked for standard claims; custom ns_scope caused a 403 in one path. Monica: please add a mapping rule or we can accept ns_scope as a fallback scope claim — prefer explicit mapping for auditing.

Action list (technical):
- K-1: implement chunking test harness and share trace with Alex by 2026-10-19. (Owner: karthik_iyer)
- M-1: propose mapping for ns_scope and share a small spec (1 page) by 2026-10-20. (Owner: monica_patel)
- P-1: add a 'tool-calling' contract example to the SDK examples repo: a 2-step RPC flow that demonstrates function-call -> model tool -> response. Deliver by 2026-10-22. (Owner: priyom_das)

FYI: I'll attach the raw smoke-run logs to the MAP hub (link in follow-up).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer (Platform Integrations), Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alex Pierce <alex@nimblesecure.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP kickoff: integration sprint status, owners, and blockers — weekly summary

Alex / team,

Thanks for the updates — quick consolidated weekly checkpoint and next steps.

Status summary:
- SDK/API: repo skeleton pushed; example bindings (JS, Py) are in review. No blocking issues. (Owner: Priyom)
- Auth/token: Monica to deliver mapping spec by EOD today. Risk: ns_scope mapping required for role-based access. (Owner: Monica)
- Streaming: Karthik's smoke test shows acceptable median latency but P95 spikes with >2MB frames; recommended client chunking. (Owner: Karthik)

Open blockers and asks for NimbleSecure:
- Provide confirmed max concurrency and typical frame sizes for each integration use case by 10/22. (Action: Alex)
- Confirm whether Nimble will accept compressed frames (gzip/deflate) or prefers chunking semantics. (Action: Alex)

Concrete next milestones and owners:
- 2026-10-19: Karthik posts chunking test results & logs. (DONE)
- 2026-10-20: Monica posts auth mapping spec. (IN PROGRESS)
- 2026-10-22: Priyom publishes MAP hub doc with owners, timelines, and sample tool-calling example. (UPCOMING)

Attachments included in MAP hub: nimble_integration_plan_v2.pdf, auth-token-specs.xlsx
MAP hub: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-nimble-map
HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/contacts/ND-4827

Let's keep the Friday 10am PT recurring slot — I will send a short agenda 24h prior. If the procurement contact needs any artifacts for their internal review (SLA, SOC2 summary), loop procurement@nimblesecure.com and I'll pull the compliance pack.

Thanks — close sync next Friday.

-priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
